ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all natural persons, corporate partners and ultimate beneficial owners against the Luxembourg FIU's reference lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council resolutions, OFAC SDN and sanctioned-list databases, and CSSF AML/CFT professional implementation guidelines; enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons, high-risk third countries and transactions linked to cash-intensive or high-risk cargo business even when the domicile is in a low-risk jurisdiction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All registrations and filings must be submitted in French, German or Luxembourgish. The chosen company name may be in any language using Latin script, provided it is linguistically distinctive and transliterated into Latin characters. The legal form indicator 'SCSp', 'S.C.Sp.' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' must appear in the name of the partnership. The name must not be contrary to public order, misleading, or likely to create confusion with any existing corporate name or trademark in the RCS.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (where use falsely suggests public or sovereign linkage)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of an official LBR name rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the RCS legal department via the Luxembourg Business Registers portal, setting out the grounds of distinctiveness and providing evidence of prior trademark or corporate name availability. The RCS will issue a reasoned decision. If the rejection is then affirmed, the applicant may bring an administrative-law action before the Tribunal Administratif within three months from the notice date. Alternatively, a secondary name may be submitted as priority reservation immediately upon receiving the rejection notice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For this unregulated low-risk parcel consolidation hub, a virtual office arrangement may be permissible provided a physical and accessible Luxembourg-registered address is maintained, mail is routinely forwarded, and statutory registers and accounting records can be inspected on site by Luxembourg authorities. The entity must nevertheless be able to demonstrate management substance, operational direction, or service-provider oversight in Luxembourg where treaty entitlements or VAT registration are claimed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified below 5% per annum for a purely non-licensed logistics vehicle; however, the likelihood increases to approximately 25% if tax-advantaged SCSp structuring is combined with perceived substance deficiencies or if the entity falls within an unannounced RCS/CSSF monitoring campaign.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (contrat de société) filed as the acte constitutif through the e-Registration portal (e-registre.lu) for entry in the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement. Contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement; no statutory escrow account or capital deposit is required at formation. General partner(s) have unlimited joint and several liability; special partner(s) risk only their agreed contribution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial general partner, acting by unanimous consent, hereby subscribes to the partnership interests allocated to it under the partnership agreement and ratifies the admission of the special partner. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Société en Commandite Spéciale be fixed at [address in Luxembourg], legally compliant and capable of receiving service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as gérant (managing partner) with sole signature authority, authorized to open bank accounts, engage employees, apply for permits, and represent the partnership before all public authorities. All actions taken prior to incorporation are ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Registered Office Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS electronic database and request a certificate of non-confusion for the proposed name suffixed with 'SCSp'. Simultaneously verify that the intended registered office is a physical address in Luxembourg and that the landlord or owner consents to registration.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of the applicant
Proof of address / utility bill for the intended registered office
Signed landlord consent if third-party premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or the address is non-compliant, submit an alternative name or a revised office address; a new request may be filed immediately without prejudice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (recommended) or the parties directly
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société) containing the parties, contributions, profit-sharing ratio, management powers, registered office, duration, and dissolution terms. Have the general partner and special partner(s) sign; where the SCSp acquires real estate or a notarial form is required by lenders, execute before a Luxembourg notary.
required_dossiers: Bank reference letter if capital contribution is by transfer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies drafting defects, amend the agreement through a private rider or re-execute; if private signature is challenged, obtain apostilled signatures and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the incorporation dossier electronically on e-registre.lu. Attach the executed partnership agreement, the gérant’s declaration of acceptance, the certificate of registered office, and the negative name certificate. Pay the registration fee online and obtain the RCS matricule number.
required_dossiers: Declaration of acceptance by the appointed gérant
Proof of payment of registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, respond within 15 days by uploading the missing document. If the filing is rejected, correct the deficiencies and resubmit with a request for priority processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA and RCS Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice – Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the Registry electronically transmits the extract for mandatory publication in the RESA. Verify the published text for accuracy and retrieve the formal RCS extract, which is a precondition for banking and tax procedures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, file a written reminder with the RCS/RESA. If the extract contains errors, request a rectification by submitting a formal correction sheet.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration form (form 10/10bis) via MyGuichet.lu to obtain a VAT number for the SCSp. Register with the ACD for municipal business tax or income tax if the SCSp is not fully transparent. If employees will be hired, register as an employer with the CCSS and social security office.
required_dossiers: UBO declaration to the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests clarification, provide the requested information by email. If VAT classification is disputed, request a written tax ruling from the Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority under the 29 December 2014 law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational Establishment Permit and Environmental Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes; Administration de l'Environnement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) for the parcel consolidation activity. Simultaneously submit an environmental registration file to the Administration de l'Environnement if the warehouse is a classified establishment. Attach building conformity certificates, fire safety plans, and site description.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or title deed of the hub premises
Fire safety certificate from the CGDIS
Environmental classification form and waste management plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business permit is refused, submit a reconsideration request to the Minister of the Economy within one month. If an environmental registration is queried, supply missing technical data and amend the file; an appeal lies to the Administrative Tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) and Autorisation de classement (environmental operating permit) for an e-commerce parcel consolidation and line-haul hub

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II Registration for standard warehousing below 5,000 m²; Category I Full EIA Report if the hub includes cold storage, hazardous goods, or generates significant traffic or emissions
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 March 2020 for wastewater discharge limits; VOC emission thresholds under Directive 2010/75/EU; waste handling and traceability obligations under the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; industrial noise limits per surrounding zoning

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Luxembourg Inland Revenue for corporate and income tax: www.impotsdirects.public.lu; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT: aedt.public.lu; business and national identification number registration via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and the Single Point of Contact at guichet.lu / rcs.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity establishing an SCSp must first file the partnership agreement, appointments and registered office details with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu. Upon RCS registration, the Luxembourg Business Registers issues a 13-digit national identification number used as the general tax reference. For VAT, if the entity makes taxable supplies in Luxembourg, Form 1610 (VAT registration application) must be filed with AEDT before trading; no local permanent establishment or physical presence is strictly required to register, but a Luxembourg VAT identification number is mandatory once registration is due. Inward/outward VAT registrations and modifications are filed electronically through the AEDT e-space.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box system. An SCSp is fiscally transparent by default and is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax; each partner is taxed directly on its allocable share. There is no general election to convert the SCSp into a corporation, but an exceptional 'opting partnership' may be possible under national private law with civil-form conversion, and VAT grouping election under Article 62 of the Luxembourg VAT Law allows an SCSp to join a VAT group with other Luxembourg taxable persons. Atad-aligned hybrid mismatch declarations and foreign classification filings must be made to the ACD where a partner's treaty treatment conflicts with Luxembourg transparency.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover, excluding VAT, for Luxembourg-established taxable persons eligible for the small business exemption; non-established foreign entities have no exemption threshold and must register from the first taxable supply in Luxembourg, subject to intra-EU distance sales thresholds under the Union OSS (EUR 10,000 per calendar year).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory digital stamping, and no API-based tax clearance for standard B2B invoices. Invoices to the Luxembourg public sector must be submitted through the Peppol network in Peppol BIS 3.0 format; B2B e-invoicing is voluntary and any structured or unstructured electronic document is valid provided the authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility are guaranteed. VAT returns and recapitulative statements are filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu or the AEDT portal, but there is no real-time pre-clearance approval of each invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for supplies of goods that are physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier or on its behalf, provided the goods leave the EU within the statutory proofs and the supplier holds the required customs export evidence. Intra-EU dispatches to a taxable person in another Member State are also zero-rated when the customer has a valid EU VAT identification number and the supplier obtains the customer's VAT number, transport document, and an intra-Community declaration in the recapitulative statement. Freight and ancillary transport services related directly to exports and services physically performed outside the EU are zero-rated if the underlying statutory conditions and documentary evidence in the Luxembourg Circular on export services are satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading, CMR, or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement of goods
Proof of payment / Inward Remittance Certificate
Signed delivery receipts or customer confirmation of receipt
EU VAT identification number validation and intra-Community purchase orders for EU zero-rating
Inward Remittance Certificate showing foreign exchange repatriation, where exported proceeds are received in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities scrutinise export zero-rating claims through documentary audits, automated risk profiling, and cross-checks against customs declarations and transport data. If the mandatory customs documentation bundle is incomplete, not retained, or not produced on request, the zero-rating is denied and the taxpayer is assessed Luxembourg VAT at 17% on the full amount plus late-payment interest and penalties, and the corresponding input VAT credits are clawed back. Where false or forged documentation is knowingly submitted, administrative penalties may be imposed and criminal proceedings may be initiated under the Luxembourg VAT Law, the General Tax Code and EU anti-fraud instruments, with fines and imprisonment applicable upon conviction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); prudential and AML/CFT supervision of banks and electronic money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), with the BCL responsible for monetary policy, payment system oversight (TARGET2, LIPS), and balance-of-payments statistics collection.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully integrated Eurozone member; capital-account convertibility is complete under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, with no exchange-control authorization for the conversion of EUR into foreign currency. Current-account profit remittances and distributions of an SCSp pass-through to non-resident partners are freely executed via SEPA or SWIFT, subject only to Anti-Money-Laundering driven source-of-funds documentation and CSSF CDD requirements. No distinction is made between capital-account and current-account convertibility in practice; barriers are limited to UBO identification, sanctions screening, and the SCSp's lack of legal personality (contractual-partnership status) which requires counterparty acceptance of a named account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender obligation exists in Luxembourg. The SCSp's cross-border parcel consolidation revenue is treated as a sale of logistics services/goods brokerage; receipts may be retained in EUR, USD, CNY, or any freely convertible currency in the entity's name, without any statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio. BCL reporting applies only for statistical balance-of-payments thresholds, and banks may record the ISIC 5229 service-payment economic purpose for regulatory filings; repatriation and conversion remain unrestricted under EU capital-movement rules.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Airwallex is rated HIGH for operational cross-border clearing: it holds EU EMI licenses passported into Luxembourg under PSD2, enabling scalable multi-currency sub-ledgers (USD, CNY, EUR, GBP), interbank-margin FX conversion, local-clearing collections (e.g., US ACH, CN cross-border sweep, SEPA instant), and direct API integration for the parcel consolidation hub's payment engine. Legal constraint: the SCSp has no legal personality, so the EMI account must be denominated in the SCSp's statutory denomination with the general partner (gérant) acting as the financial signatory; despite this, larger Luxembourg financial institutions may refuse to recognize EMI receipts as bank-confirmation evidence for capital verification and commercial LC issuance. Therefore the viable architecture is a dual-rail strategy: a Tier-1 a domestic bank for escrow, LC, and audit-grade confirmation, plus Airwallex as the high-velocity operating-clearing rail. Regulatory watch: CSSF Guidance and the Loi du 12 novembre 2004 (AML) require that the EMI perform full UBO verification of the SCSp's partners; use of a dedicated SCSp sub-account rather than a personal account of the general partner is mandatory to preserve legal separation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML regulation does not impose a statutory physical-presence interview; however, Tier-1 domestic banks (BIL, Banque de Luxembourg, Société Générale) enforce in-practice on-site KYC meetings with the general partner (gérant) and any individual holding at least 10% of the SCSp, unless a fully notarized and apostilled dossier (passport, proof of address, partnership agreement, RBE extract, bank reference letter) is combined with a certified video-call identity confirmation performed under CSSF Circular 12/02 standards. Non-EU partners without a Luxembourg nexus will almost always trigger a physical-first onboarding. Remote opening is fully feasible for Airwallex and most EMIs, requiring only digital identity verification (iDen, e-passport NFC, liveness) and submission of the same corporate bundle. Recommended defense: assemble a CSSF 12/02-compliant onboarding pack prior to application, including apostilled certified copies dated within 6 months, and schedule a virtual pre-meeting with the KYC officer to pre-clear the pass-through structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp classified as a contractual arrangement without legal personality, raising doubts on bank-account title and signatory capacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS (Luxembourg Register of Commerce) extract demonstrating optional registration; notarized partnership agreement (contrat de société) expressly authorizing the account opening; CSSF-compliant resolution of the general partner appointing authorized signatories; VAT certificate (LU-linked) and Economic-Interest declaration; RBE registration extract proving the SCSp is recorded with beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity through the limited-partner chain of a pass-through vehicle withholding partner identities from the bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO table (full legal name, DOB, nationality, tax residence, percentage of capital and profit entitlements) for each natural person behind all direct and indirect partners; organizational chart of the ownership chain; sworn statement of no additional BO; Regime-de-Bénéficiaires-Effectifs (RBE) filing confirmation submitted to the Luxembourg Business Registers; written consent letters from partners allowing banks to conduct politically exposed person (PEP) and sanctions screening without triggering data-protection claims.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, low-ticket cross-border e-commerce settlement flows (large number of 10–80 EUR parcel disbursements and platform sweep-ins) misidentified as unlicensed payment services or money remittance business
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial master service agreements proving the ISIC 5229 freight-forwarding/consolidation model; signed contracts with e-commerce platforms and marketplace sellers; operational invoices showing the parcel-handling fee structure; customs EORI records and airway-bill proofs of physical linehaul; transfer logs showing funds are consideration for logistics services, not customer-to-customer payments; a written legal opinion from a Luxembourg attorney confirming the activity is exempt from PSD2 payment-services licensing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, restrictive-measures, and adverse-media exposure triggered by non-EU counterparties on the China–US–Europe parcel trade lane
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated daily sanctions-screening logs covering EU Consolidated List, UN sanctions, OFAC SDN/SSI and Non-SDN lists; Chinese entity counterparty DDQs and WFOE evidence; WorldCheck negative-news and PEP reports for every partner and director; a sanctions-compliance manual registered with the Luxembourg Commissariat aux sanctions financières (CSF); contractual clauses mandating re-screening of all merchants and last-mile carriers; a no-transaction-with-listed-persons certification under Luxembourg law of 19 December 2020.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds uncertainty for the initial equity injection routed from a non-resident e-commerce holding company into the SCSp, creating a suspected tax-avoidance or unexplained-wealth red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized capital contribution and subscription form (no minimum capital requirement for SCSp); audited balance sheet of the parent proving surplus; loan/equity agreement with commercial pricing; bank reference letter from the originating jurisdiction confirming the remitter; MT103/SEPA transfer record with ISO purpose code EQUI; Luxembourg transfer-pricing documentation compliant with the 2021 Luxembourg TP Decree; confirmation that no conversion or round-tripping is involved; an explanatory memorandum on the business purpose of the consolidation-hub capital structure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Preferred routing is a SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 credit using the ISO financial purpose code EQUI (equity injection) or GCAP (general capital transfer), instructed on the Luxembourg Tier-1 account; SEPA Credit Transfers may alternatively be used for intra-EEA contributions with structured remittance referencing the executed subscription pledge. Bank-side verification follows CSSF CDD rules: aggregated contribution statement for the SCSp (without filing a capital-liability certificate), notarized subscription form, traceable source of funds from the non-resident entity, and RBE update within 15 days of a partner change; for retained foreign-currency injection, the receiving bank will register the conversion at the prevailing ECB reference rate and may request the underlying commercial rationale for the USD/CNY working capital build-up. An Airwallex inbound mirror account is recommended only for pre-financing float; ultimate capital attested for audit and distribution purposes should pass through the domestic bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement rails are tiered by value and destination: (1) high-value linehaul charters and airplane belly-space procurements cleared via SWIFT MT103 with ISO purpose code GDDS (paid goods and services) in EUR or USD; (2) for medium-value cross-border carrier contracts, a documentary Commercial Letter of Credit issued by Société Générale Luxembourg or BIL with documents-against-acceptance terms, enabling bank confirmation of the freight payment against airway-bill presentation; (3) EU last-mile couriers and hub staff paid via SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant (< EUR 100,000, settled in seconds on the clearing rail); (4) destination-side terminal fees and customs duties discharged through local clearing rails in each country (FedEx/UPS consolidated billing, US ACH/Same-Day ACH for the US inbound zone, CN Cross-Border Payment settlement accounts for Chinese last-mile partners); (5) float optimization via the Airwallex multi-currency treasury: USD and CNY collections are consolidated, converted at interbank-tightened spreads, and released only against verified delivery-event triggers to prevent duplication and wire-fraud exposure.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNY) with a Luxembourg credit institution or Airwallex under an ISDA/CSA master agreement, covering the parcel hubs' expected 90-day settlement exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on CNY restricted to the offshore CNH market, permissible for hedging the China-lane procurement-cost exposure without requiring onshore deliverability or PRC FX approvals
Cross-currency swap (EUR/USD notional exchange) for re-aligning the revenue currency of the US injection channel to the euro-denominated operating cost base of the Luxembourg warehouse network

Vanilla FX options (EUR call / USD put and EUR call / CNY put) for asymmetric protection against air-freight fuel surcharge volatility and unexpected tariff-driven rate moves, purchased with the treasury policy limit set at 1.5% of quarterly revenue

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Owners (RBE confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the anniversary of the SCSp's entry in the RBE; LBR sends an annual reminder and confirmation is effected via the RBE e-file portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation triggers a formal reminder with an administrative fee of EUR 125; repeated non-compliance can lead to administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 and criminal sanctions (imprisonment from 1 month to 5 years and/or fines) for knowingly inaccurate declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts and Audit Report Filing (if not exempt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of approval of the annual accounts; approval must occur within six months of the balance-sheet date. For a calendar-year SCSp, the accounts must be filed by 31 July at the latest.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after a formal summons carries a penalty of EUR 100 per day or up to EUR 10,000; continued delay can result in a criminal fine up to EUR 50,000, appointment of a mandatory auditor, and the non-opposability of the accounts to third parties. Persistent non-compliance for several years may lead to administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) from the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a Luxembourg-approved réviseur d'entreprises agréé is mandatory for an SCSp that exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: (i) balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; (ii) net turnover EUR 8.8 million; (iii) average employees of 25. An audit is also required if the SCSp is a public-interest entity, a collective-investment undertaking under CSSF supervision, a securitisation company, or if the partnership agreement expressly imposes one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The SCSp's annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with Luxembourg GAAP (Luxembourg Law of 19 December 2002, as amended). IFRS is mandatory for listed undertakings and is permitted as an alternative for non-public-interest unlisted entities; for the cross-border e-commerce parcel consolidation hub, Luxembourg GAAP is the default standard for statutory financial statements in the RCS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Luxembourg law of 13 January 2019, the SCSp's general partner (associé commandité) or a registered agent must, within one month following each anniversary of the RBE registration, electronically confirm the exact beneficial-ownership information displayed in the RBE. This annual confirmation is not a transfer filing; any direct or indirect transfer of partnership interests that changes the beneficial ownership of the SCSp (i.e., natural persons owning or controlling more than 25% of the SCSp) must be reported by an amendment to the RBE within one month of the date of transfer. The amended details are then covered by the annual confirmation at the next anniversary.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 – USD 20,000 per year (only if audit thresholds are exceeded; otherwise EUR 0)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% standard CIT (unchanged for tax year 2025); plus 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT, producing a 18.19% national effective CIT rate for corporate partners. In Luxembourg City the municipal business tax rate of 6.75% applies, bringing the combined marginal corporate tax burden to approximately 24.94%. The SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not itself subject to CIT; tax is borne by the partners on their allocable share of profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is pass-through eligible: no entity-level corporate income tax, no municipal business tax and no net wealth tax at the partnership level. Corporate partners may access: (i) participation exemption - 100% exemption on qualifying dividend income (10% participation or EUR 1,200,000 lower acquisition-cost threshold) and qualifying capital gains (10% participation or EUR 6,000,000 threshold), in both cases with a 12-month holding period and subject to the 2018 anti-abuse conditions; (ii) Luxembourg IP box - 80% deduction of net qualifying intellectual property income and capital gains, producing an effective combined rate of approximately 5%; (iii) unlimited carryforward of tax losses; and (iv) no domestic WHT on interest and royalties.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited - Luxembourg tax law (Article 114 LIR) imposes no statutory expiry date on tax losses of a Luxembourg business or on the allocable share passed through the SCSp to partners. A 17-year cap was contemplated in the 2024-2025 tax reform package but has not been enacted into force. Loss carryforward is available only where the business is not interrupted; on a change of control, the 12-month continuation rule under Article 114(2) LIR applies.
